description: Chromium is a steely-grey, lustrous, hard, and brittle transition metal with atomic number 24 and symbol Cr, representing the first element in group 6 of the periodic table.
uses: Chromium is valued for its high corrosion resistance and hardness, with major applications including the production of stainless steel and chrome plating through electroplating, which together comprise 85% of commercial use. It is also greatly valued for its ability to be highly polished while resisting tarnishing, reflecting almost 70% of the visible spectrum and 90% of infrared light.
characteristics: Chromium is the third hardest element after carbon and boron with a Mohs hardness of 8.5, has a melting point of 1907 °C and boiling point of 2671 °C, and exhibits unique antiferromagnetic ordering at room temperature. In air, chromium forms a thin protective surface layer of chromium oxide that enhances its corrosion resistance, and it is highly resistant to tarnishing unlike metals such as copper, magnesium, and aluminium.
